site.name: Tru Nobility
site.description: Clothing, history, ideas and tools for people building something bigger.

hero.headline: History isn’t something we just remember.
hero.accent: It’s something we study, carry, teach and wear.
hero.body: Tru Nobility is evolving from a clothing brand into a home for history, culture, art and education. Through clothing, storytelling and free teaching resources, we’re building new ways to explore the people, ideas and movements that still matter.
hero.imageAlt: Tru Nobility community member in a library wearing a history-inspired shirt

freedomStudies.seriesBody: History is more useful when we ask what people actually did with it.
freedomStudies.episodeSubtitle: Music. Freedom. Another Way to Imagine.
freedomStudies.episodeBody: Before we get into the mythology, the costumes and the claims about Saturn, let’s start with the artist underneath it all—and just how enormous the body of work actually is.
freedomStudies.quote: Space is not an escape from life, but a deeper way of living it.
freedomStudies.imageAlt: Sun Ra looking upward in mirrored glasses and an ornate metallic costume

featuredResource.label: OUR MISSION IS GROWING
featuredResource.title: Bringing life to our history lessons
featuredResource.body: Tru Nobility began by helping people wear the history. Now we’re creating free educational resources that help teachers, families and students study it, question it and carry it forward.
featuredResource.imageAlt: Preview pages from a free Tru Nobility classroom resource
points: Free PDFs to download and share
featuredResource.quote: Education is a form of freedom.

articles.label: From the written archive
articles.title: Read. Learn. Go deeper.
articles.intro: Long-form essays make room for questions that need more than a caption. We explore the history, ideas and cultural context behind the people and movements that matter.

items.title: What July 4th Feels Like When You Know Too Much
items.summary: A personal examination of national myth, public ritual and what freedom means when the celebration and the history do not agree.
items.imageAlt: A July Fourth meal arranged over a copy of the Declaration of Independence

items.title: Our Art Used to Be a Language: The Hidden Meaning of African Mudcloth
items.summary: How Bogolanfini carries history through material, symbol and visual proverb—and what it asks of descendants learning to read it.
items.imageAlt: Black, ochre and brown African mudcloth pattern

support.title: If this gave you something, help us make the next one.
support.body: Tru Nobility’s educational work takes research, writing, recording, design and production. If you’ve learned something here—or used one of our resources—you can help us keep building them.
support.aside: Buying a shirt, sharing a lesson, following the work, and telling somebody about us help too.

footer.tagline: History works better when we do.
